models.label: wav2vec2-base phoneme CTC — INT8 (default)
models.notes: wav2vec2-base (94.4M params, bookbot/wav2vec2-ljspeech-gruut) fine-tuned for IPA phoneme CTC output. Dynamic INT8 quantization applied to MatMul/Gemm ops only — the 7-layer conv feature extractor and the positional conv embedding stayed FP32 because their weight-norm reparameterization (a Mul feeding Conv) isn't a quantizer-recognized constant initializer. FP32 source was 377.8MB; this build is 121.9MB (32%).

models.label: wav2vec2-base phoneme CTC — FP32 (diagnostic)
models.notes: Same checkpoint, no quantization. Added 2026-08-01 specifically to test one hypothesis: real-iPad WebGPU steady-state latency on the INT8 build came back at ~572ms (mean, post-warmup, tight variance 540-631ms) — over 3x the sandbox's own INT8-on-CPU number. INT8 kernels are far more mature on WASM/CPU than on current WebGPU backends across browsers; it's plausible INT8 is actively hurting here (dequantize-around-matmul overhead, or partial CPU fallback) rather than helping. If FP32 is faster than INT8 on WebGPU specifically, that confirms it and changes the quantization strategy; if FP32 is also ~500ms+, the bottleneck is elsewhere (e.g. per-op GPU dispatch overhead across 12 transformer layers at this sequence length) and quantization isn't the lever to pull.
